```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# I want to run something like 
# run_rmd_chunk("analysis/bg.Rmd", "main-loop")
# later

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(here)
here()

run_rmd_chunk <- function(file, label, envir = globalenv()) {
  lines <- readLines(file)

  start <- grep(
    sprintf("^```\\{r[[:space:]]+%s([,[:space:]]|\\})", label),
    lines
  )

  if (length(start) != 1L) {
    stop("Chunk label not found or is not unique: ", label)
  }

  end <- which(seq_along(lines) > start & lines == "```")[1]

  if (is.na(end)) {
    stop("Closing code fence not found.")
  }

  eval(
    parse(text = lines[(start + 1L):(end - 1L)]),
    envir = envir
  )
}
```

This page presents the mathematical foundation of the proposed ebpmf-background model.

# Section 1: ebpmf-background problem formulation
Let ${\bf X} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{n \times p}$ denote a matrix of observed counts $x_{ij} \in \mathbb{R}$. Background Poisson NMF parameters include ${\bf L} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{n \times K}$, ${\bf F} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{p\times K}$, and $\bf f_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^p$ and we seek values of ${\bf L}$, ${\bf F}$, $\bf f_0$ such that ${\bf X} \approx ({\bf L}{\bf F}^T) \text{diag}({\bf f_0})$. In the progress, we will also update ${\boldsymbol \pi} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{M \times K}$.

$$
\begin{align}
x_{ij} &\sim \mathrm{Pois}(\lambda_{ij}) \\
\lambda_{ij} &= f_{j0} \sum_{k=1}^K l_{ik} f_{jk} \\
f_{jk} &\sim g_k, \qquad 
g_k = \sum_{m=1}^M \pi_{mk} \text{Gamma}(\text{shape} = a_m, \text{rate} =a_m) \\
f_{j0}, f_{jk}, 
l_{ik}, \pi_{mk} &\geq 0, \qquad 
\sum_{m=1}^M \pi_{mk}=1
\quad \text{for each } k
\end{align}
$$

We use the same Poisson latent variable formulation as in ebpmf-gamma, modified to include the background term $f_{j0}$:

$$
x_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^K z_{ijk},
\qquad
z_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Pois}(f_{j0}l_{ik}f_{jk}).
$$
The latent variable formulation remains essentially the same, with the main changes being the feature-specific background factor $\bf f_0$, and now $\pi_{mk}$ is the optimization objective while $a_m$ remains fixed.

In addition, we maintain the assumption for mean field variational distribution $q(\mathbf{Z},\mathbf{F}) = q(\mathbf{Z})q(\mathbf{F})$. This is the only assumption we make for the posterior.

# Section 2: EBPMF-BG ELBO Update

### Section 2.1 Update $\boldsymbol \pi$

Introduce a latent mixture indicator
$\delta_{jk}\in\{1,\ldots,M\}$, with

$$
p(\delta_{jk}=m\mid \boldsymbol \pi)=\pi_{mk}.
$$

Here, we regard $\delta_{jk}$ as the hidden component assignment for $f_{jk}$, and $\pi_{mk}$ is the prior probability that $f_{\cdot k}$ belongs to component m. Note $\pi_{mk}$ is shared across all j.

Variational posterior probability that component $m$ generated $f_{jk}$ can be called "responsibility":
$$
r_{jkm}
=
q(\delta_{jk}=m)
$$

These responsibilities are updated in the $q(F,{\boldsymbol \delta})$ update in Section 2.2 and are held fixed when updating $\boldsymbol \pi$.To see how responsibilities enter the $\boldsymbol \pi$ update, begin with the full ELBO for the indicator-augmented model:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{L}
&=
\mathbb{E}_q\Big[
\log p(Z\mid L,F,f_0)
+ \log p(F\mid\delta)
+ \log p(\delta\mid\pi) \\
&\qquad\qquad
- \log q(Z)
- \log q(F,\delta)
\Big]
+ \mathrm{const}.
\end{aligned}
$$

During the coordinate update for $\pi$, the variational distribution $q$ and the model parameters other than $\pi$ are held fixed. Consequently, $\log p(\delta\mid\pi)$ is the only term in the full ELBO that changes with $\pi$. All remaining terms can be absorbed into a constant:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\pi}
=
\mathbb{E}_q[\log p(\delta\mid\pi)]
+ \mathrm{const}.
$$

Because each $\delta_{jk}$ is categorical, its probability can be written
using indicator variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(\delta_{jk}=m\mid\pi)
&=
\pi_{mk} \\
&=
\prod_{m=1}^{M}
\pi_{mk}^{\mathbf{1}\{\delta_{jk}=m\}} \\
\log p(\delta\mid\pi)
&=
\sum_{j=1}^{p}
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\sum_{m=1}^{M}
\mathbf{1}\{\delta_{jk}=m\}\log\pi_{mk}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Taking the expectation replaces each indicator by its variational probability:

$$
\mathbb{E}_q\!\left[
\mathbf{1}\{\delta_{jk}=m\}
\right]
=
q(\delta_{jk}=m)
=
r_{jkm}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{L}_{\pi}
&=
\sum_{j=1}^{p}
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\sum_{m=1}^{M}
r_{jkm}\log\pi_{mk}
+ \mathrm{const}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For each factor $k$, define the expected component count for simplicity:

$$
N_{mk}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{p}r_{jkm}.
$$

The coordinate update for $\pi_{\cdot k}$ therefore solves

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underset{\pi_{\cdot k}}{\operatorname{maximize}}
\quad&
\sum_{m=1}^{M}N_{mk}\log\pi_{mk} \\
\text{subject to}\quad&
\pi_{mk}\geq 0,
\qquad
\sum_{m=1}^{M}\pi_{mk}=1.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is a multinomial maximum-likelihood problem with soft
component counts. Its solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pi_{mk}^{\mathrm{new}}
&=
\frac{N_{mk}}{\sum_{h=1}^{M}N_{hk}} \\
&=
\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{p}r_{jkm}}{p},
\end{aligned}
$$

because $\sum_{m=1}^{M}r_{jkm}=1$ for every feature $j$ and factor $k$.

<!-- In finite-precision arithmetic, repeated updates can drive an unused component
below the smallest representable positive number. The implementation therefore
solves the same multinomial M-step with the additional numerical constraint
$\pi_{mk}\geq\epsilon$, using $\epsilon=10^{-12}$. Components whose unconstrained
weights fall below $\epsilon$ are fixed at the boundary, and the remaining
probability mass is distributed among the free components in proportion to
their expected counts. This keeps `log(pi)` finite while preserving an exact
coordinate maximizer over the constrained simplex. -->


### Section 2.2 Update $q(F,\delta)$
The Gamma-mixture indicator is explicit in this update. For each
$f_{jk}$, use the variational factorization

$$
q(f_{jk},\delta_{jk})
=
q(f_{jk}\mid\delta_{jk})q(\delta_{jk}),
$$

where

$$
q(\delta_{jk}=m)=r_{jkm}.
$$

The implementation stores these responsibilities as `resp[j, k, m]`. Define for simplicity the expected allocated count  $C_{jk} = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}_q[z_{ijk}]$ and exposure $D_{jk}=f_{j0}\sum_{i=1}^{n}l_{ik}$.

For a fixed mixture component $m$, the coordinate ascent variational inference (CAVI) update is

$$
\begin{aligned}
q^*(f_{jk},\delta_{jk}=m)
&\propto
\exp\Bigg\{
\mathbb{E}_{q(Z)}
\left[
\log p(Z_{\cdot jk}\mid L_{\cdot k},f_{jk},f_{j0})
\right]
+\log p(f_{jk}\mid\delta_{jk}=m)
+\log p(\delta_{jk}=m\mid\pi)
\Bigg\} \\[4pt]
&\propto
\exp\Bigg\{
\underbrace{
C_{jk}\log f_{jk}-D_{jk}f_{jk}
}_{\text{likelihood terms involving }f_{jk}}
+
\log\left[
\frac{a_m^{a_m}}{\Gamma(a_m)}
f_{jk}^{a_m-1}
\exp(-a_mf_{jk})
\right]
+\log\pi_{mk}
\Bigg\} \\[4pt]
&\propto
\pi_{mk}
\frac{a_m^{a_m}}{\Gamma(a_m)}
\underbrace{f_{jk}^{a_m+C_{jk}-1}
\exp\left[-(a_m+D_{jk})f_{jk}\right]}_{\text{kernel of Gamma(shape =} a_m + C_{jk}, \text{rate = } a_m + D_{jk} )}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Define for simplicity

$$
\alpha_{jkm}=a_m+C_{jk},
$$

$$
\beta_{jkm}=a_m+D_{jk},
$$

the updated Gamma shape and rate. The unnormalized joint factor can then be
written as

$$
q^*(f_{jk},\delta_{jk}=m)
\propto
\widetilde r_{jkm}
\operatorname{Gamma}
\left(f_{jk};\alpha_{jkm},\beta_{jkm}\right),
$$

Integrating the unnormalized joint kernel over $f_{jk}$ gives the component
responsibility up to a common normalization constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde r_{jkm}
&\propto
\int_0^\infty
q^*(f_{jk},\delta_{jk}=m)\,df_{jk} \\
&\propto
\pi_{mk}
\int_0^\infty
\operatorname{Pois}(C_{jk};D_{jk}f_{jk})
\operatorname{Gamma}(f_{jk};a_m,a_m)
\,df_{jk} \\
&\propto
\pi_{mk}\,
\widetilde{\operatorname{NB}}
\left(
C_{jk};
\operatorname{size}=a_m,\,
\operatorname{prob}=
\frac{a_m}{a_m+D_{jk}}
\right).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\widetilde{\operatorname{NB}}$ denotes an NB-shaped Gamma--Poisson
marginal score. It is not necessarily an ordinary negative-binomial
probability mass because $C_{jk}$ is an expected count and can be fractional.
The implementation evaluates the equivalent Gamma-function expression on the
log scale for numerical stability.

Normalizing over mixture components gives

$$
r_{jkm}
=
\frac{\widetilde r_{jkm}}
{\sum_{h=1}^{M}\widetilde r_{jkh}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
q(\delta_{jk}=m)=r_{jkm},
$$

and

$$
q(f_{jk}\mid\delta_{jk}=m)
=
\operatorname{Gamma}
\left(f_{jk};\alpha_{jkm},\beta_{jkm}\right).
$$

The moments required by the $q(Z)$, $L$, and ELBO calculations are

$$
\mathbb{E}_q[f_{jk}]
=
\sum_{m=1}^{M}
r_{jkm}\frac{\alpha_{jkm}}{\beta_{jkm}},
$$

and

$$
\mathbb{E}_q[\log f_{jk}]
=
\sum_{m=1}^{M}
r_{jkm}
\left[
\psi(\alpha_{jkm})-\log\beta_{jkm}
\right].
$$

### Section 2.3 Update q(Z)

The CAVI update is

$$
q^*(Z)
\propto
\exp\left\{
\mathbb{E}_{q(F,\delta)}
\left[\log p(Z\mid L,F,f_0)\right]
\right\}.
$$

Conditional on $X_{ij}=\sum_k Z_{ijk}$, the factor allocations follow

$$
q(Z_{ij\cdot})
=
\operatorname{Multinomial}
\left(X_{ij};\phi_{ij1},\ldots,\phi_{ijK}\right),
$$

where

$$
\phi_{ijk}
=
\frac{
l_{ik}\exp(\mathbb{E}_q [\log f_{jk}])
}{
\sum_{h=1}^{K}l_{ih}\exp(\mathbb{E}_q [\log f_{jk}])
}.
$$

The factor $f_{j0}$ cancels because it is shared across $k$ for a fixed
feature $j$.

### Section 2.4 Update L

Holding other parameters fixed, the $L$-dependent ELBO is

$$
\mathcal{L}_L
=
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\left[
\left(\sum_{j=1}^{p}\overline z_{ijk}\right)\log l_{ik}
-
l_{ik}\sum_{j=1}^{p}f_{j0}\mathbb{E}_q [f_{jk}]
\right]
+ \mathrm{const}.
$$

Setting its derivative to zero gives the maximizer

$$
l_{ik}^{\mathrm{new}}
=
\frac{
\sum_{j=1}^{p}\overline z_{ijk}
}{
\sum_{j=1}^{p}f_{j0}\mathbb{E}_q [f_{jk}]
}.
$$

### Section 2.5 Update $f_0$

Similar to 2.3 and 2.4, olding other parameters fixed, the $f_0$-dependent ELBO is

$$
\mathcal{L}_{f_0}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{p}
\left[
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\overline z_{ijk}\right)
\log f_{j0}
-
f_{j0}
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{k=1}^{K}
l_{ik}\mathbb{E}_q [f_{jk}]
\right]
+ \mathrm{const}.
$$

Because $\sum_k\overline z_{ijk}=X_{ij}$, define for simplicity:

$$
y_j=\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_{ij},
\qquad
A_j
=
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}l_{ik}\right)\mathbb{E}_q [f_{jk}].
$$

Maximizing $y_j\log f_{j0}-A_jf_{j0}$ gives

$$
f_{j0}^{\mathrm{new}}
=
\frac{y_j}{A_j}.
$$
